info.title: Attome XRM API
info.description: The Attome XRM platform's HTTP API. Entity record shapes under `/api/v1/{entity}` are resolved from each deployment's runtime metadata (D-003) and therefore cannot be enumerated statically — those operations document the generic envelope only. Fetch `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields.

get.description:
The workflow definitions that are not deleted, optionally only active or inactive ones, one-based
pages. Automation administrators only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based: page 1 is the first page.

post.description:
A definition with a unique logical name and a kind (`flow` by default, or `journey`, `nurture`,
`sequence`; fixed once created). It has no version yet. Recorded in the open changeset.
Automation administrators only. Audited.

409.description: A workflow with this logicalname already exists, or no open changeset to record into

get.description: One definition with its versions. Automation administrators only.

delete.description:
Marks it deleted and inactive, so it starts no more runs. Recorded in the open changeset.
Automation administrators only. Audited.

409.description: No open changeset to record into, or the workflow is owned by another layer

patch.description:
Renames it or switches it on or off when `row_version` is the stored one. Recorded in the open
changeset; another layer's definition is 409. Automation administrators only. Audited.

409.description: row_version mismatch, no open changeset to record into, or the workflow is owned by another layer

post.description:
A new draft version, numbered after the highest, with the graph given (an empty graph
otherwise). Recorded in the open changeset. Automation administrators only. Audited.

409.description: Another version is being created, no open changeset to record into, or the workflow is owned by another layer

get.description: One version: its number, status (draft or published) and graph. Automation administrators only.

patch.description:
Replaces the graph of a draft version when `row_version` is the stored one, so two editors cannot
overwrite each other; a published version or a stale version is 409. Recorded in the open
changeset. Automation administrators only. Audited.

409.description: row_version mismatch or not a draft, no open changeset to record into, or the workflow is owned by another layer

post.description:
Checks the graph (no cycles, ports of matching types) and refuses a bad one with what is wrong,
then makes the draft the published version and rebuilds its triggers in the same transaction.
Recorded in the open changeset. Automation administrators only. Audited.

409.description: Not a draft, another publish in progress, no open changeset to record into, or the workflow is owned by another layer

post.summary: Replay a version over recent runs
post.description: Replays a version over the flow's latest finished runs (M4-T3): each run's trigger input and approval decisions go through the simulation of this version, and every node whose outcome differs from what the run really did is reported. Nothing is written.

x-audit-exempt.note: M4-T3: replays a draft through the D-431 simulation only; it reads past runs and writes nothing.

post.description:
Runs the version's graph in memory against the trigger payload given and returns every node's
trace. Nothing is written, sent or requested, whatever the nodes are, and a draft that is still
being edited can be simulated. Automation administrators only.

x-audit-exempt.note: D-431: this module executes a workflow graph purely in-memory and may never perform a real database write, entity mutation, notification dispatch, webhook call, or approval request under any node type — nothing here has a persistent effect to audit.

get.description:
Runs newest first, optionally only one status or only the runs about one record, one-based pages.
Automation administrators only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based: page 1 is the first page.

post.description:
Starts the published, active version of the workflow named, with the context given and
optionally the record it is about. Automation administrators only. Audited.

get.description:
One run: its version, status, context, node data and each step's runs (round, status, attempts,
last error). Automation administrators only.

post.description:
Cancels a queued, running, waiting or paused run when `row_version` is the stored one; a finished
or changed run is 409. Automation administrators only. Audited.

post.summary: Move a run to another version
post.description:
Moves a waiting or paused run to a published version of its flow, each waiting step to the step
of the same id; a step missing from the target is 422. Send the run's `row_version`. Automation
administrators only. Audited.

200.description: The run now belongs to the target version

409.description: The run is not waiting or paused, or changed since it was read

422.description: A waiting step is missing from the target version

get.summary: Preview moving a run to another version
get.description:
Where each waiting step of the run would land in the target version (a published version of the
same flow). Changes nothing. Automation administrators only.

parameters.name: target_version_id
parameters.description: The version to move the instance to.

200.description: Where each waiting step lands in the target version

422.description: The target is not a published version of the same flow

post.description:
No step of a running or waiting run runs until it is resumed. Send the run's `row_version`.
Automation administrators only. Audited.

200.description: The run is paused; no step runs until it is resumed

409.description: The run is not running or waiting, or changed since it was read

post.description:
The run continues where it stopped. Send the run's `row_version`. Automation administrators only.
Audited.

200.description: The run continues; a step still waiting keeps waiting

409.description: The run is not paused, or changed since it was read

post.description:
Runs a failed run again from its failed step, with that step's attempts reset, when `row_version` is
the stored one. Automation administrators only. Audited.

200.description: The run continues from its failed step, with the inputs it had

409.description: The run is not failed, or changed since it was read

get.description:
D17-T2: the published, active sequences a rep can enrol contacts in,
with what ends them and how many contacts are in each now.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
One-based (D-347): page 1 is the first page. Values below 1 are
clamped up to 1 rather than rejected, matching the legacy lists.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description:
Rows per page, clamped to `1..=MAX_PAGE_SIZE`. Defaults to
`DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`.

post.description:
Name the contacts, or give a marketing list of contacts (as you see it).
Each contact gets one run of the sequence; a contact already active in it
is skipped. The contact leaves the sequence when they reply, a meeting
with them is booked, or a deal at their account changes stage (as the
sequence's `settings.sequence.exit_on` says).

200.description: The contacts are enrolled and their runs started

404.description: No published, active sequence with this name

422.description: No contacts, more than 1,000 named or 10,000 in a list, a list of other records, or the sequence's exits are invalid

get.description:
The change-feed events whose workflow entry triggers the dispatcher gave up on, with the last
error, one-based pages. Automation administrators only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
One-based (D-347): page 1 is the first page. Values below 1 are
clamped up to 1 rather than rejected, matching the legacy lists.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description:
Rows per page, clamped to `1..=MAX_PAGE_SIZE`. Defaults to
`DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`.

delete.summary: Discard a workflow trigger dead letter
delete.description:
Drops the event from the dead letters without starting anything. Automation administrators only.
Audited.

post.summary: Replay a workflow trigger dead letter
post.description:
Starts the entry triggers the event matches again; a trigger that already started for the event
is not started twice. Automation administrators only. Audited.

200.description: Replayed; the dead letter is removed

503.description: Dispatch is overloaded or a dependency is unavailable; the dead letter is kept

ControlBody.description: A control request: the instance's current `row_version`.

ControlResult.description: The instance's state after a control action.

kind.description:
D17-T1: `flow` (the default), `journey`, `nurture` or `sequence`.
Fixed once created.

owner_layer.description: Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this workflow.

EnrolBody.description: The contacts to enrol: named, or a marketing list's (D17-T2).

list_id.description:
A marketing list of contacts, as the caller sees it (at most
[`MAX_LIST`] people), instead of `contact_ids`.

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `customer_tests_failed`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`request_rejected`, `invalid_cursor`, `resync_needed`, `cascade_restricted`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

errors.description:
Every field-level failure on a `validation_error`, as
`{attribute, rule, message, fix}`.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

instance.description: The request path the problem happened at.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

retryable.description:
Whether the same request may succeed later (the error catalogue's
verdict for `code`).

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

title.description:
A short title for `code` in the request's language (Z14-T3), e.g.
`The resource was not found.`

type.description: Z14-T1 (RFC 9457): `about:blank`; the problem is named by `code`.

ExitOn.description: Why a contact leaves a sequence.

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

LockedField.description:
One field a business rule locks for the writer (D-789 §3.5): `effect` is
`hidden` or `disabled`. No value is ever echoed.

MoveBody.description: Move a run to another version of its flow.

MoveMapping.description: One waiting step and where it lands in the target version.

found.description: The node exists in the target version with the same type.

NodeDifference.description: One node whose outcome differs between a real run and the draft.

draft.description:
The node's status in the draft's simulation; `None` when the draft
never reached it (or removed it).

real.description:
The node's status in the real run; `None` when it never ran there
(or the draft added it).

input.description:
The node's input and output; absent for a large pair kept in object
storage (`payload_ref`) or a node that has not run.

payload_ref.description: The object-storage key of a large input/output pair.

round.description: M3-T1: the loop round (0 outside a loop).

PaginatedResponse_DefinitionListItem.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

owner_layer.description:
Solution 7 (D-785): the layer that owns this workflow — `platform`,
`product`, `project` or `customer`. Only a changeset of that layer may
change, publish or retire it.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_InstanceListItem.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_SequenceSummary.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

items.description: A published sequence, as a rep picks it (D17-T2).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_TriggerDeadLetter.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

attempts.description: Failed dispatch attempts that were counted.

last_error.description: The last counted failure, as the dispatcher logged it.

operation.description: `create`, `update`, … as written to the change feed.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

differing.description: Runs with at least one difference.

ReplayRequest.description: M4-T3: the request: how many of the flow's latest finished runs.

ReplayedRun.description: One real run replayed through the draft.

RuleFailure.description:
One business-rule `error` policy that fired (D-789 §3.3), inside a
`rule_violation` body's `details.rules`. Carries names and the rule's own
message, never a record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RuleViolationDetails.description:
`details` of a `rule_violation` response (D-789): the field of the first
failing policy, when it names one, and every blocking `error` policy that
fired, the first (by rule display order) being the one `rule_id` names.

status.description:
`workflow_node_run.status` vocabulary — `succeeded`, `skipped`,
`waiting` (this branch would have suspended for real), or `failed`.

taken_port.description: Set only for `Condition`/`Approval` — which output port fired.

would_have.description:
Human-readable description of the real side effect this node would
have performed outside a dry run — present only for a node whose
live executor has one (D-431: this is the only thing standing in for
it, never the effect itself).

SimulateRecordRef.description: M4-T1: the record a simulation reads.

approval_decisions.description:
`node_id -> "approved" | "rejected"`, consulted by an `Approval` node
reached during the simulated run instead of filing a real
`attome_approval` request. A node with no entry here defaults to
`"approved"` so a simulate run doesn't dead-end at the first
approval gate a caller didn't think to pre-decide.

oneOf.description:
M4-T1: a real record to run the flow against. It is read as the
person simulating (record access and field grants apply) and handed
to the trigger as `{entity, record_id, record}` merged over
`trigger_payload`. Nothing is written.

trigger_payload.description:
Fed to the graph's entry `Trigger` node exactly as a real trigger
context would be — see `instance_admin::start_instance_internal`'s
`context` for the live equivalent.

status.description:
`completed` (every reachable node settled), `would_wait` (the run hit
a node that would have suspended for real — `WaitForEvent`/
`SubWorkflow`, or a `Wait` past the iteration bound), or `failed`.

dispatched.description:
Workflow instances this replay newly started; 0 when every trigger
the event matches had already started. Waits are never resumed.

Warning.description:
Something the server did that the caller should know about though the
request succeeded (a value truncated, a default applied, a page clamped):
a stable `code` and English `message`. Sent only when there is one.

WorkflowMovePreview.description: What moving the run would do.

movable.description: Every waiting step is found in the target version.

portal_session.name: __Secure-wp_{portal}_session
portal_session.description: A web portal user's session cookie, issued by the portal's sign-in; `{portal}` is the portal's keyword (`wp_{portal}_session` on plain-http local dev). Valid only on that portal's own routes.

s2s_hmac.name: x-s2s-signature
s2s_hmac.description: A system-to-system call, signed. Send `x-s2s-client-id`, `x-s2s-key-id`, `x-s2s-timestamp` (Unix milliseconds, within 300 seconds of the server's clock), `x-s2s-nonce` (single use: a repeat is refused) and `x-s2s-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the hex-decoded client secret, of `METHOD`, `PATH_AND_QUERY`, the hex SHA-256 of the body, `TIMESTAMP` and `NONCE`, joined by newlines in that order.

session_cookie.name: __Host-session_token
session_cookie.description: Browser session cookie issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Mutating requests additionally require the CSRF conditions enforced by `middleware::csrf`.
